blocks.text: Setting up your Notion workspace for community management

The secret to using Notion effectively is starting with a simple database. Community managers often deal with fragmented information. You might have member emails in one place and social media drafts in another. Start by creating a central database for your projects. Press ⌘ N to create a new page, then type /database to select a board view. This board view acts as your command center for community tasks.
How to manage community tasks on Mac

When you have many tasks, use the filter function. Click the Filter button at the top of your database. Filter by status to see only pending items. This keeps your view clean. If you need to find a specific member entry, use ⌘ P to open the search bar. Type the member name and hit Enter. This saves you from scrolling through long lists.
Faster with Lazur: your Mac assistant

Lazur helps you stay in the flow while using Notion. If you forget where a specific setting is, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur. For example, ask 'Where is the share button?' and Lazur will point at it on your screen. This is helpful when you are working in a complex database layout.

You can also use Lazur to dictate content directly into a Notion block. Hold the fn key and start talking. Your spoken words appear as formatted text. This is great for capturing ideas after a community call. You do not need to pause and type manually. This keeps your momentum going throughout the day.
Practical Notion tips for community managers

items: Use templates for recurring tasks like onboarding new members. Go to the arrow next to the blue New button in your database and select Create a template.
Add a callout block to highlight important community guidelines. Type /callout to create a visually distinct area.
Use a toggle list to hide long pieces of content. Type /toggle to create a collapsible section for notes.
Link to other pages using the @ symbol. Type @ followed by the page name to create a quick reference.

blocks.text: Community managers often need to export data for reports. Notion makes this easy. Click the three dots in the top right corner of any page. Select Export. You can choose PDF or Markdown format. If you need to bring in data from a spreadsheet, use the import feature. Go to the sidebar and click Import, then select CSV.

One common mistake is creating too many sub-pages. This makes it hard to find information later. Keep your workspace flat where possible. Use tags within your databases to organize items instead of nesting pages deep inside each other. Another mistake is ignoring keyboard shortcuts. Learning just five shortcuts will change how you use the app. Press Shift + ? to see the full list of shortcuts anytime.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant that helps you find buttons, guide you through steps, and dictate text. It does not click buttons or edit files directly.

faq.question: What is the best way to track member feedback in Notion?
faq.answer: Create a database with a select property for feedback type and a date property. Use the board view to group entries by status.

faq.question: Does Notion require an internet connection?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion is a cloud-based app. You need an active internet connection to sync your pages and databases.

faq.question: How do I check if my Mac is compatible with the latest Notion app?
faq.answer: Notion requires macOS 13 or later. You can check your version by clicking the Apple menu in the top left corner and selecting About This Mac.
